title: Minimax Regret under Evidence Constraints When Personalization Gain Equals Implementation Cost
banked_reason: Sound incremental deployment-regret separation substitutes for the unachieved connected-confidence-interval frontier; field floor missed and independent validity audit identified no bounded same-topic repair.
gap_reasons: This delivers a non-sharp evidence-constrained policy-regret separation, not the promised sharp connected versus arbitrary confidence-interval values, least-favorable interval geometry, or attaining interval sequence for the causal personalization gain.

The unresolved sharp object is itself a different composite-null deployment problem introduced by the core; the supplied positioning concedes the proved bounds neither improve a stated prior theorem nor characterize the consumer's K-fold procedure.

The delivered note replaces the requested confidence-interval connectedness frontier with deployment regret at a public implementation-cost boundary, proving no interval-length value, connectedness comparison or attaining interval sequence.
Neither the composite-null optimizer nor scalar sufficiency is determined, and the sufficient dual certificate is never instantiated with matching measures and a feasible kernel.
proof_attempt_summary: The connected-interval angle retained local geometry and information-bound calculations but produced neither a continuum-certified connectedness separation nor lossless connectedification, leaving the sharp interval values, least-favorable geometry and original-data interval attainment open. The pivot instead derived an internally reviewed Gaussian and original-Bernoulli deployment-regret gap above 4/25 and a feasible scalar evidence gate; its constrained optimizer and scalar sufficiency remain unresolved. D0.5 rejected that substituted kernel at incremental tier, and an independent validity gate found no bounded repair of the original topic; no Lean formalization was reached.
tldr: At the supplied public center, gross personalization gain is \(1/5\), equal to the implementation cost. Two personalized and two common policies therefore compete on the same local welfare scale. A uniform ten-percent evidence constraint forces maximal scaled regret above \(33/50\), while a concrete empirical welfare selector has maximal regret below \(1/2\), throughout \(H\in[29/10,31/10]\). The regret gap exceeds \(4/25\). The comparison retains all five Gaussian observations and persists for every randomized evidence-constrained procedure using the original Bernoulli records. Neither regret value is claimed sharp; the constrained optimizer and scalar-gate question remain unresolved.
gap: Scalar innovation comparisons explain why significance testing need not minimize regret. They do not determine the optimal evidence-constrained policy choice when the personalized and common menus are both unknown.
fill: A full-menu separation theorem supplies a quantitative welfare penalty, and a composite-null variational question isolates the optimal policy partition and the possible failure of scalar gain gating.
